tool.description: Manage Microsoft DNS servers: zones, records (IPv4 and IPv6), reverse lookup, aging/scavenging and a full configuration check.
tool.long_description: Connects to one or more Microsoft DNS servers – domain controllers with AD-integrated zones as well as standalone servers outside a domain – with the current account, stored credentials or a different login. Every zone opens in its own tab with all records (A, AAAA, CNAME, PTR, MX, TXT, SRV, NS and read-only display of all other types), general settings (dynamic updates, aging, zone transfers, notify) and its findings. Creating or changing an A/AAAA record keeps the matching PTR record in the reverse zone (IPv4 and ip6.arpa) in sync. New zones (primary, AD-integrated, secondary, stub, conditional forwarder) are created from a dialog, including IPv6 reverse zones. The check finds missing or orphaned PTR records, CNAME conflicts, dangling targets, duplicate addresses, risky zone settings (non-secure updates, transfers to any server, aging off), stale records and compares NS servers and forwarders by querying them (SOA serial, response). A scavenging preview shows which dynamic records would be deleted and whether the device still answers to ping. Optionally reads leases and reservations from a Microsoft DHCP server and compares them with DNS (missing, wrong or orphaned records). Search across all zones and servers, compare zones between servers, server settings, cache and the DNS server audit log with reading aids. With several servers connected, a column shows per record whether it has already replicated to the others, and replication can be triggered on demand (AD replication of the DNS partition or zone transfer to secondary servers). Changes made by others are detected through the SOA serial; every change runs as a transaction and is undone automatically if a step fails. Talks to the server via WMI (root\MicrosoftDNS) – no PowerShell or RSAT needed.

bulk.static_q:
Make {n} dynamic records static? They then no longer age and are not scavenged.

{list}
chk.a_no_ptr: {name} ({ip}) has no PTR record in the reverse zone.
chk.aging_no_scavenging: Aging is on for zone {zone}, but scavenging is off on the server – nothing is deleted.
chk.aging_off: Zone {zone} accepts dynamic updates but aging is off – stale records are never removed.
chk.aging_off_dynamic: Zone {zone} contains dynamic records but aging is off – stale records stay forever.
chk.aging_short: Zone {zone}: no-refresh + refresh is only {hours} h – clients with longer DHCP leases or switched-off devices lose their records. Common: 7 + 7 days.
chk.cache_pollution: {server}: protection against cache pollution is off.
chk.cname_apex: Zone {zone} has a CNAME record for the zone itself – not allowed.
chk.cname_chain: CNAME {name} points to {target}, which is itself a CNAME (chain).
chk.cname_conflict: {name} has a CNAME record and further records ({types}) – not allowed, clients get unpredictable answers.
chk.cname_dangling: CNAME {name} points to {target}, which does not exist.
chk.cname_multiple: {name} has more than one CNAME record.
chk.dns_no_lease: {name} ({ip}) is dynamic and lies in a DHCP scope, but there is no lease or reservation – probably stale.
chk.dup_ip_dynamic: {name} has the same address {ip} as {other} (newer) – probably stale.
chk.insecure_updates: Zone {zone} allows nonsecure dynamic updates. Outside a domain this is often needed – restrict access to the server where possible.
chk.insecure_updates_ad: Zone {zone} is AD-integrated but allows nonsecure dynamic updates – any client can overwrite records. Use "Secure only".
chk.lease_no_dns: DHCP lease {name} ({ip}) has no A record.
chk.no_forwarders: {server}: no forwarders – external names are resolved via the root hints.
chk.no_ns: Zone {zone} has no NS record for the zone itself.
chk.no_reverse_zones: {server}: no reverse lookup zones – PTR lookups (nslookup, logs) fail.
chk.notify_off: Zone {zone} has secondary servers but notify is off – they only learn about changes at the next refresh.
chk.ns_lame: Zone {zone}: name server {ns} is not authoritative for the zone (lame delegation).
chk.ns_no_answer: Zone {zone}: name server {ns} does not answer ({error}).
chk.ns_serial: Zone {zone}: name servers have different serials – newest {serial}, behind: {behind}.
chk.one_forwarder: {server}: only one forwarder – if it fails, no external names can be resolved.
chk.probe_ns_tip: Sends DNS queries (SOA) to every name server of a zone and to the forwarders: reachable, authoritative, same serial.
chk.ptr_multiple: {ip} has {n} PTR records ({names}) – reverse lookup returns any of them.
chk.ptr_partial: {name} is not a complete reverse name (no full address).
chk.ptr_stale: PTR {ip} points to {target}, but {target} has the address {have}.
chk.ptr_target_missing: PTR {ip} points to {target}, which does not exist.
chk.scav_multiple: Scavenging is on at several domain controllers ({servers}) – one per domain is enough.
chk.scavenging_off: {server}: zones with aging exist, but scavenging is off.
chk.scavenging_often: {server}: scavenging runs every {hours} h – once a day or less is enough.
chk.soa_expire: Zone {zone}: the SOA expire time is not longer than the refresh interval.
chk.soa_minimum: Zone {zone}: the minimum TTL (negative caching) is {ttl} – missing names stay unresolvable for a long time.
chk.soa_retry: Zone {zone}: the SOA retry interval is longer than the refresh interval.
chk.stale_record: {name} was not renewed for {days} days (aging is off).
chk.stale_summary: Zone {zone}: {n} dynamic records are stale or will be soon – see Scavenging.
chk.state: {server} checked at {time} in {sec} s – {zones} zones, {records} records.
chk.state_partial: Check of {server} cancelled at {time} after {sec} s – {zones} zones, {records} records checked.
chk.target_is_cname: {rtype} record {name} points to {target}, which is a CNAME – the target must be a host name with an address.
chk.target_missing: {rtype} record {name} points to {target}, which does not exist.
chk.target_no_address: {rtype} record {name} points to {target}, which has no A/AAAA record.
chk.ttl_zero: {name} has TTL 0 – answers are not cached.
chk.underscore: {name} contains an underscore – not allowed in host names (RFC 952/1123), some clients reject it.
chk.wildcard: {name} is a wildcard record – it answers for every name that does not exist.
chk.with_dhcp_tip: Reads leases and reservations from a Microsoft DHCP server and compares them with the A records.
chk.xfer_any: Zone {zone} allows zone transfers to any server – anyone can download the whole zone.
chk.xfer_list_empty: Zone {zone} allows transfers only to listed servers, but the list is empty.
chk.zone_empty: Zone {zone} contains no records apart from SOA and NS.
chk.zone_not_everywhere: AD-integrated zone {zone_name} is missing on: {servers} (other replication scope?).
chk.zone_paused: Zone {zone} is paused – the server does not answer queries for it.
chk.zone_settings_diff: Zone {zone_name} has different update/aging settings on the servers.
chk.zone_shutdown: Zone {zone} is shut down – the server does not answer for it (e.g. transfer from the master failed or the zone expired).

help.text:
MS DNS Extended Management – quick help

OVERVIEW
  All zones of the selected server with type, storage, dynamic updates, aging, transfers and findings.
  Double-click opens a zone in its own tab. "New zone …" creates forward and reverse zones (IPv4 and IPv6).
  Several DNS servers can be connected at once (e.g. all domain controllers or standalone servers).

ZONE TAB
  Records: all records of the zone. A, AAAA, CNAME, PTR, MX, TXT, SRV and NS can be created and changed,
  other types are displayed. With an address record the matching PTR record is kept in sync.
  General: SOA, dynamic updates, aging, zone transfers, notify and zone actions (reload, transfer, pause …).
  Findings: errors, warnings, best practice and information. Double-click runs the suggested fix or jumps to the record.
  Scavenging: which dynamic records the next scavenging would delete, with ping and DHCP state.

SERVER, SEARCH, COMPARE
  Server: forwarders, recursion, scavenging, advanced settings, cache and forwarder test.
  Search: names, addresses or networks across all loaded zones of all servers.
  Compare: server settings and zones between the connected servers, SOA serials per server.

CHECK
  Checks all zones of the server, optionally queries the name servers and forwarders and compares with a
  Microsoft DHCP server (leases and reservations).

CHANGES BY OTHERS
  Before saving, the SOA serial of the zone is compared. If someone else changed the zone, the tool shows
  what changed and who (audit log). Every change runs as a transaction and is undone if a step fails.
  Deleting a zone cannot be undone.

login.intro: MS DNS Extended Management manages Microsoft DNS servers – domain controllers with AD-integrated zones as well as standalone servers outside a domain – via WMI (root\MicrosoftDNS), like the DNS console. IPv4 and IPv6. No PowerShell and no RSAT needed.
login.no_cred: No stored credentials selected or they could not be fetched.
login.requirements: Requirements: membership in "DnsAdmins" or local administrators on the server, and remote WMI/DCOM access (RPC, port 135 plus dynamic ports). For a server outside the domain use "Other credentials" with SERVER\user. The local server is used with the logged-on account (Windows does not allow other credentials locally).

repl.denied:
AD replication from {server} ({part}) was denied: the account {user} lacks the right "Replication Synchronization" on the partition {part}. By default Domain Admins have it (for ForestDnsZones: Enterprise Admins); it can also be delegated.

The remaining steps were carried out anyway. Without this right the change arrives with normal AD replication: within a site usually after seconds to a few minutes, between sites according to their schedule.
